subject: Error when using non- intercept only state formula in occuMulti

messages.author: 135451aadffb8d7f
messages.subject: Error when using non- intercept only state formula in occuMulti
parts:
Hi, I'm getting an error when I try to include state formulas. I try to run

specList <- list(mink = as.matrix(minkMatr),
                 otter  = as.matrix(ottMatr),
                 pine_marten = as.matrix(martMatr),
                 red_fox = as.matrix(foxMatr))

obscovlist <- list(time = as.matrix(cov_time))

sitecovs <- as.data.frame(cbind(cov_relProp, cov_trap)) %>%
  rename(relPropUnknown = `cov_relProp` ,trap = `cov_trap`) %>%
  mutate(relPropUnknown = logit(relPropUnknown,F), trap = as.logical(trap))

OMDat <- unmarkedFrameOccuMulti(specList, sitecovs, obscovlist, maxOrder = 2)

OMFit <- occuMulti(detformulas = c('~ trap + relPropUnknown','~ trap + relPropUnknown','~ trap + relPropUnknown', '~ trap + relPropUnknown'),
                       stateformulas = c('~time','~1','~1','~1','~1','~1','~1','~1','~1','~1'),
                       data = OMDat,
                       maxOrder = 2)

This gives the error:

Error in model.frame.default(sf_no0[[i]], site_ref) :
  object is not a matrix

Does anyone know what I'm doing wrong?

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Error when using non- intercept only state formula in occuMulti
parts:
You have specified time as an observation-level covariate. You can't include it in a state formula - only site-level covariates (in your sitecovs) can be in the state formulas.

Ken

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Error when using non- intercept only state formula in occuMulti
parts:
Population closure is a key assumption of occupancy models. That is, the model assumes the occupancy state of both species is not changing from one replicate sample to the next. If that's the case for you, you probably need to shrink down the total time covered by your sequence of samples/encounter history (e.g. from a month to a week) so that you can reasonbly assume occupancy is stable during that time.

If you specifically want to model the changes in occupancy over time for the first species, you should use a dynamic occupancy model or a "stacked" approach where you treat site-time periods as sites (search this forum for "stacking" for more information). There is a dynamic version of the multispecies model (Fidino et al 2019), but this is not supported by unmarked.

Ken
